title: Banking System Vulnerability: 2026 Update - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed's annual US banking vulnerability update (data to 2026:Q2): three of four measures are rising — the 2008-redux capital gap jumped to $16.9bn from $1.9bn as capital ratios slipped (2022-redux gap $151.1bn, compounded by rate increases since March 2026), fire-sale and run vulnerability are up and above 2015–22 lows, and the liquidity stress ratio is at its highest since 2014 — though all remain below pre-2008 levels.

insights.claim: Under the NY Fed's '2008 redux' stress scenario, the US banking system's aggregate capital gap to a 10% Tier 1 common equity ratio rose to $16.9 billion in 2026:Q2 from $1.9 billion a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: A ~9x rise from a low base signals erosion in bank capital buffers — watch for weaker buybacks/dividend capacity.
insights.quote: under the “2008 redux” scenario, the capital gap stands at $16.9 billion (up from $1.9 billion in 2025:Q2)
insights.locator: These indexes have been stable or increasing

insights.claim: Under the NY Fed's '2022 redux' rate-shock scenario, with unrealized AFS and HTM securities losses fully reflected in capital, the bank capital gap is $151.1 billion, little changed from $161.3 billion in 2025:Q2.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Interest-rate risk on securities books remains the dominant capital vulnerability — banks stay sensitive to further rate rises.
insights.locator: These indexes have been stable or increasing

insights.claim: NY Fed researchers attribute the rise in capital vulnerability to declining bank capital ratios, compounded in the rate scenario by the generalized increase in interest rates since March 2026.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Rising rates in 2026 are re-opening the unrealized-loss channel that drove the 2023 banking turmoil.
insights.locator: These recent shifts can be explained

insights.claim: Bank starting capital, including unrealized securities gains and losses, had improved since 2023, but since 2025:Q2 there are early signs of a trend reversal with capital deteriorating modestly.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Inflection in bank capital trend is an early warning for bank equity and credit spreads.
insights.quote: there are early signs of a trend reversal, with capital levels deteriorating modestly
insights.locator: The chart below documents the decomposition

insights.claim: The NY Fed's Fire-Sale Vulnerability Index is slightly higher than a year ago, on an unsteady uptrend since late 2024, moderate historically but elevated versus 2015–2022, with changes driven mainly by fair-value leverage.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Leverage is the lever to watch for fire-sale amplification risk in a shock.
insights.locator: The Fire-Sale Vulnerability Index is slightly higher

insights.claim: The NY Fed's bank Liquidity Stress Ratio has risen since 2022:Q1 to its highest level since 2014, slightly above half its 2007:Q3 peak, driven by fewer liquid assets plus more unstable funding and off-balance-sheet exposures.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Thinner liquidity buffers raise sensitivity to deposit outflows — relevant for regional bank risk and Fed liquidity facilities.
insights.quote: currently stands at a level not seen since 2014
insights.locator: The first chart in this post shows

insights.claim: The NY Fed's Run Vulnerability Index has risen versus last year, elevated relative to 2015–2022, with higher illiquid assets, unstable funding and stress leverage all contributing.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Run risk is building across multiple components — a reason to monitor uninsured deposit concentrations.
insights.locator: The Run Vulnerability Index has increased

insights.claim: Three of the NY Fed's four banking vulnerability measures show increasing trends; all remain below pre-2008 crisis levels but some are higher than the lows of 2015–2020.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: Not a crisis signal, but a deteriorating trend in systemic bank resilience that amplifies any macro shock.
insights.quote: three of our four measures show increasing trends in vulnerabilities of the overall banking system

insights.claim: The NY Fed tracks banking-system fragility with four complementary measures from FR Y-9C data — capital gap (CLASS stress model), fire-sale spillovers, liquidity stress ratio and run vulnerability — capturing how capital, fire-sale, liquidity and run risks interact to amplify shocks.
insights.speaker: Matteo Crosignani
insights.so_what: A reusable dashboard for systemic bank risk; each component maps to a distinct crisis channel.
insights.locator: How Do We Measure Banking System Vulnerability?
